en.attentionVisible: Also alert "needs you" while the window is in front
en.attentionVisibleHint: Alert even while the window has focus. Turn off to hear only once the window goes to the background (another app, covered, or minimised).
en.autoDismissHint: An alert that arrived while you were away should still be there when you return. "Keep while away" only tidies up while the page is in front.
en.autoFocus: Click a toast to open that conversation
en.autoFocusHint: A click switches to the conversation the alert came from; off means a click does nothing.
en.blurb: Get told when the agent needs your input, or when a reply finishes in the background.
en.bridgeOff: Quick-decision buttons are unavailable right now (
en.bridgeOffDesktop: dsh-app:// pages cannot register a Service Worker (the shell does not grant the allowServiceWorkers privilege), and a system notification carries no Approve / Reject buttons: the approval alert still pops, click it to open the conversation and decide.
en.bridgeOffTail: ); this notification carries no buttons — click it to open the conversation and decide.
en.currentQuiet: Stay quiet for the conversation on screen
en.currentQuietHint: A wait belonging to the conversation on screen keeps only the tab marker, so the page is not covered; moving the window to the background or stepping away from it restores alerts.
en.donePolicyHint: "Quiet for the open one" means the conversation you are reading finishes silently while any other conversation still alerts — useful with several conversations open.
en.enableHint: When off: no toasts, no sounds, and the tab title is left alone.
en.externalAttentionHint: Push approval / plan review / question alerts to the external endpoints too.
en.externalDoneHint: Push reply-finished alerts to the external endpoints too.
en.externalEmpty: No push targets yet — press "Add target" to create one.
en.externalEnableHint: Master switch: when off, nothing is sent to any external endpoint.
en.externalHint: Also push alerts to Discord / Bark / Gotify / custom webhooks, so you hear about it away from the machine. Same trigger rules as local alerts.
en.externalNoTargets: Add at least one push target first.
en.externalOffHint: Turn on "Forward to external targets" first.
en.externalPrivacy: The alert title and body (including the session name and snippet) are sent as-is to the address you enter — only use endpoints you trust.
en.externalTargetsHint: Add as many as you like. Discord: the webhook URL; Bark: https://api.day.app/<device key> (self-hosted: http://<server>/<key>); Gotify: https://<server>/message?token=<app token>; custom: any endpoint accepting JSON (POST: source / event / title / body / sessionId / time).
en.externalTestHint: Send one test message to every push target above (the per-kind forward toggles do not apply to this button).
en.hostEnvDesktopForcedNote: (this page is not dsh-app://: a toast click will try to launch the dsh:// protocol and the browser may show an "open app?" prompt)
en.hostEnvHint: Auto-detect by default: a dsh-app:// page is the Desktop (DSH Desktop) shell, anything else is the Web. Override it if detection comes out wrong: on the Desktop a toast click fires the dsh:// deep link (the effect is unreliable) and system notifications carry no Approve / Reject buttons; on the Web it is window.focus() plus the Service Worker bridge.
en.offHint: Reminders are off: enable them first, then test.
en.permHint: Notification permission is not granted yet — click once on the page and allow notifications so toasts can appear (sound is unaffected).
en.permHintInline: Not granted yet — allow it once from the page.
en.quickActionsHint: Approval notifications carry Approve / Reject; one click settles the request without switching back. Needs a Service Worker browser (http://127.0.0.1 or https); where it cannot run (the Desktop shell) the alert is a plain notification without buttons — clicking it opens the conversation.
en.quickApprovalNote: "Approve" equals "Allow once" in the conversation — it allows that one call only.
en.resetHint: Put every option above back to its default (picked sound files included).
en.soundCleared: Custom sound removed; this alert falls back to the built-in cue.
en.soundHint: Master cue switch; what it plays comes from Advanced → Alert sound.
en.soundNotAudio: That is not an audio file this browser can play.
en.soundOffHint: The Sound switch is off: turn it on to preview (with it off the alerts themselves stay silent too).
en.soundPreviewSystem: The system sound plays with a toast, not from the plugin — a test alert was sent instead; that sound is it.
en.soundQuota: Not enough browser storage for this file — remove the other kind's custom sound first, or pick a smaller file.
en.soundSourceHint: Each alert kind picks its own source; the two never affect each other. Default is the built-in cue.
en.soundSynthNote: The plugin's synthesized cue — "needs you" and "reply finished" use different patterns.
en.soundSystemNote: No plugin cue: the toast still appears, but the sound is left to the operating system, so its timbre follows your system notification settings. The Sound switch above still mutes it.
en.soundTooBig: File is too large; the limit is
en.subagentQuietHint: Skip sessions spawned by a subagent (the parent conversation covers them); the one you have open still alerts.
en.testApprovalNoBridge: Test alert sent: Desktop notifications carry no buttons — click it to open the conversation and decide.
en.testHint: Send one of each with the current settings; the "When to alert" switches are bypassed.
en.testNeedsQuick: Turn on "Decide approvals from the toast" above to test the buttons.
en.toastHint: Through the system notification center; needs notification permission, and on the Desktop these carry no Approve / Reject buttons.
